root.name: Scotch Game: Paulsen Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Nxd4 Qh4 5. Nf5

overview: After the Steinitz 4...Qh4, White plays 5.Nf5 attacking the queen and threatening Nxg7+. Black usually captures e4 with check or retreats the queen, leading to tactical complications. I am not sure of the main continuation, so the evidence is limited.

white_ideas.idea: Use the knight on f5 and quick development to attack g7 and the queen

black_ideas.idea: Take e4 with check and trade queens or retreat the queen

typical_structures.structure: Open centre, knight on f5 and exposed queens

character.notes: Early queen play and tactics on g7 and e4.

gambit.notes: White may lose the e4 pawn, but compensation is rapid development.

sublines_that_differ.name: Steinitz 5.Nb5
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Nxd4 Qh4 5. Nb5
sublines_that_differ.how: The more usual and calmer main line.

character.reason: Early queen attacks and threats on g7 lead to forcing play.

gambit.reason: Black can take e4 with check and keep it if White does not regain it.

soundness.reason: Probably inferior to the main Steinitz lines.

structure.reason: Central pawns are exchanged and lines open for pieces.

plans.reason: Both queens appear early and one has to avoid attack.
